claims.implementation: backend/arkali/evidence/artifact/content_address.py and records.py. Identity IS the content address: register() takes bytes and returns the address, and no function in the context accepts an artifact_id argument, so a producer cannot name what it is producing. hash_algorithm and digest are stored alongside the composed artifact_id. Immutability is an ORM before_update refusal on all three tables, not a convention - there is no update path at all, because bytes that changed are a different artifact with a different address. 'Versioned' has two axes and docs/contracts/artifact.md section 1 keeps them apart: content addressing versions the byte sequence, semver versions the contract shape. Full metadata is the eleven canonical items of MS section Artifact Fabric, mapped column by column in docs/contracts/artifact.md section 4.

claims.implementation: backend/arkali/evidence/artifact/store.py::ProvenanceInput and ArtifactStore.register, with backend/arkali/evidence/artifact/records.py::ArtifactProvenanceRecord and ArtifactParentEdge. Registration is ONE operation: bytes, descriptor, provenance and parent edges are recorded together, so an artifact cannot exist without the provenance VDC section Provenance requires for exactly the artifacts this store is for. ProvenanceInput is a value object rather than a mapping, so a missing item is a TypeError at the call site instead of a silently absent column. Parents are foreign-keyed edges, so a provenance chain cannot cite an artifact that was never registered.
